newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU ministers favour protocol on public broadcasting.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers favour protocol on public broadcasting.

text.p: European Union culture ministers came out on Tuesday in favour of attaching a protocol on the need for public service broadcasting to the EU treaty under revision in the inter-governmental conference.
The preference for a protocol reflects the fact that there is scant time left to revise the treaty itself by the time the conference winds up, as it is scheduled to do in Amsterdam in June.

At issue is the need to finance public broadcasting, which EU member states do through a variety of ways from state aid to television licences, while fitting in with the rigours of EU competition policy.

Dutch State Secretary for Education, Culture and Science Aad Nuis said revising the treaty itself seemed unfeasible as different member states had different conceptions of what public broadcasting actually should be and in a treaty revision it would have to be very precisely defined.
